newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher on Southwest heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher on Southwest heat.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open higher Thursday on forecasts of hot weather and resulting air conditioning demand in the U.S. Southwest, industry sources said.
"The forecast is calling for some heat in the Southwest," said one New York-based futures trader.
Temperatures in the Southwest were expected to be near-normal in the northeast to about five degrees above normal in the southwest through the weekend.
Maximum temperatures in Phoenix were expected to be near 105 degrees Fahrenheit Friday, with overnight lows near 76 degrees.
In early over the counter discussion, July Palo Verde (PV) was pegged at $30.80-31.25 from Wednesday's NYMEX July futures close at $30.31 per megawatt hour (MWh).
July California Oregon Border (COB) was assessed at $23.00-23.50 in early over the counter talk from Wednesday's NYMEX settlement at $22.69 per MWh.
Electricity futures closed lower Wednesday amid expectations several thousand megawatts of idled generation would be returning to service over the next week or so.
The focus was on about 3,000 MW of coal-fired generation scheduled to return through next week as spring maintenance is completed.

An unplanned outage at the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Palo Verde nuclear power plant in Arizona continued Thursday, although the outage was expected to be short-lived. Arizona Public Service had said it expected to restart the unit Wednesday.
Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear power unit remained off line for refueling.

In addition to the Palo Verde and Diablo Canyon nukes, several units were expected to return to service by Monday, including a 750 MW unit at Colstrip in Montana, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners in Arizona, a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger in Wyoming and a 400 MW unit at the Bonanza plant in Utah.
As of 1015 EDT the July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas contract was trading down 4.1 cents at $2.275 per million British thermal units.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were expected to be three to four degrees above normal through the weekend with scattered showers primarily through the weekend.
